title: Subjuntivo
theme: Mandative subjunctive (suggest/insist/demand that he be), past subjunctive (were across persons), "lest", fossilised subjunctive
goal: Student uses base-form subjunctive after triggers, deploys "were" for hypothetical mood, and recognises formal-literary subjunctive in writing.
module_chunks: I suggest that he be / go / take...
It is essential that he be present
It is important that she go now
They insist (that) we be on time
God save the Queen / Long live the king (fossilised)

units.title: I suggest that he be
units.grammar_focus: Mandative subjunctive after verbs (suggest, recommend, propose, demand, insist, require, request, ask)
units.real_life_context: You write formal recommendations, motions, or policy that requires base-form verbs regardless of person.

grammar.sentence: The board insists that he _____ resign immediately.
grammar.explanation: Mandative subjunctive after "insist that" — base form ("resign") regardless of subject. "He resigns" would be plain indicative. The subjunctive registers the demand. Note: in modern British English, "should resign" is often substituted ("insists that he should resign"); American English keeps the bare subjunctive.

grammar.sentence: I recommend that she _____ for the position.
grammar.explanation: "Recommend that + subject + base form". "She applies" would be indicative (no subjunctive force); "apply" carries the recommendation. Same triggers: suggest, propose, demand, request, require, insist, urge.

grammar.sentence: They demanded that the meeting _____ postponed.
grammar.explanation: "Be" is the bare subjunctive of "to be" — invariant across persons. "Was postponed" would be indicative past, weakening the demand. "Be postponed" — formal, mandative.

grammar.sentence: The committee suggested that he was more careful with the budget.
grammar.hint: After "suggest that", use base form — not past indicative
grammar.answer: The committee suggested that he be more careful with the budget.
grammar.explanation: "Was" is indicative — it describes how he was, not what's being suggested. Subjunctive "be" carries the suggestion that he should be more careful going forward. Classic C1 trap.

grammar.passage: The motion was carefully worded. 'It is recommended that the chair step down at the next meeting, that an interim be appointed, and that the by-laws be reviewed within ninety days.' The bare subjunctives — 'step down', 'be appointed', 'be reviewed' — gave the document its quietly forceful tone.
grammar.question: What does the motion recommend?
grammar.answer: the chair step down, an interim be appointed, the by-laws be reviewed
grammar.explanation: Three mandative subjunctives: "step down" (base form of step), "be appointed", "be reviewed". All triggered by "It is recommended that". Subjunctive layered for institutional formality.

listening_speaking.text: I suggest that he be more careful.
They demand that she resign.
It is essential that we act now.
I recommend that you take the train.
The judge ordered that the report be filed by Friday.

units.title: It is essential that
units.grammar_focus: Subjunctive after impersonal expressions of necessity/importance
units.real_life_context: You write academic/business prose where formality demands subjunctive after evaluative adjectives.

grammar.sentence: It is essential that the report _____ on time.
grammar.explanation: "It is essential/important/vital/crucial/imperative that + subject + base form". Here "be" (subjunctive of "to be"). Universal across persons. Indicative "is" weakens the necessity.

grammar.sentence: It is important that she _____ heard.
grammar.explanation: "It is important that she be heard" — bare subjunctive in passive form ("be + past participle"). Compare with indicative "she is heard" — different mood, different force.

grammar.sentence: It was imperative that the troops _____ before dawn.
grammar.explanation: "It was imperative that + subject + base form". Note: even when the main clause is past ("was imperative"), the subjunctive in the that-clause stays in base form. No backshift.

grammar.sentence: It is necessary that he is on time.
grammar.hint: Necessity triggers subjunctive — base form, not indicative
grammar.answer: It is necessary that he be on time.
grammar.explanation: "Is" is indicative present; "be" is the subjunctive form needed after "It is necessary that". Common slip — speakers default to "is/are" out of habit.

grammar.passage: The protocol was unambiguous. 'It is vital that all personnel be briefed before deployment. It is crucial that no detail be omitted from the report. It is imperative that the chain of command be respected at every step.' Procedural language at its most formal.
grammar.question: What three things does the protocol demand?
grammar.answer: all personnel be briefed before deployment, no detail be omitted from the report, the chain of command be respected
grammar.explanation: Three stacked "It is [vital/crucial/imperative] that + subject + be + past participle" — passive subjunctive used for impersonal formality. Procedural writing leans heavily on this register.

listening_speaking.text: It is essential that we act now.
It is vital that he be present.
It is crucial that no one be left behind.
It is imperative that the protocol be followed.
It is important that she feel welcome.

units.title: I wish I were
units.grammar_focus: Past subjunctive "were" across all persons (wishes, if-clauses, would rather)
units.real_life_context: You maintain formal correctness with "were" (not "was") in hypothetical/wish contexts.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ taller.
grammar.explanation: Past subjunctive uses "were" for ALL persons (I, he, she, it, we, you, they). "I wish I was taller" is heard in casual speech but considered non-standard in formal English. "Were" is the correct subjunctive form.

grammar.sentence: If she _____ here, she'd know what to do.
grammar.explanation: Second conditional with "she" — formal English keeps "were". Casual speech accepts "was", but the subjunctive proper is "were" universally.

grammar.sentence: I'd rather you _____ smoke in the house.
grammar.explanation: "I'd rather + subject + past simple" for preference about another person's behaviour. Strictly speaking, "didn't smoke" is the past subjunctive form here — same surface as past simple, but mood is hypothetical.

grammar.sentence: If I was you, I would accept the offer.
grammar.hint: Subjunctive "were" universal in formal "If I _____ you"
grammar.answer: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
grammar.explanation: "If I was you" is non-standard. "If I were you" is the formal correct form across all registers above casual speech. Note: in some informal native speech, "was" persists, but C1 writing demands "were".

grammar.passage: Stevens watched the rain pool on the gravel drive. 'If only it were summer,' he said, 'and if I were ten years younger, I would walk to the village without a coat. I wish I were the kind of man who didn't notice weather. But I am not, and never was.'
grammar.question: What three things does Stevens wish?
grammar.answer: that it were summer, that he were ten years younger, that he were the kind of man who didn't notice weather
grammar.explanation: Three stacked subjunctive "were" forms — formal, literary register. Note final "I am not, and never was" — switches back to indicative for present/past fact.

listening_speaking.text: I wish I were taller.
If she were here, she'd handle it.
If I were you, I'd stay.
I wish it were summer.
He acts as if he were the boss.

units.title: Lest, So be it
units.grammar_focus: Subjunctive after "lest" (formal-archaic) and fossilised expressions ("Be that as it may", "Come what may", "So be it", "Suffice it to say")
units.real_life_context: You recognise and occasionally deploy literary or archaic subjunctive forms.

grammar.sentence: Speak softly, lest you _____ the baby.
grammar.explanation: "Lest" = "in case... should" / "so that... not". Always followed by base-form subjunctive. "Lest you wake the baby" = so that you don't wake the baby. Highly formal-literary.

grammar.sentence: _____ as it may, the project must move forward.
grammar.explanation: "Be that as it may" is a fossilised subjunctive phrase = "regardless of that". Used to acknowledge an objection while overruling it. Note inverted base form "be" at the start — relic of older subjunctive syntax.

grammar.sentence: _____ what may, I will see this through.
grammar.explanation: "Come what may" = whatever happens. Another fossilised subjunctive — base form "come" without subject. Means "let what comes come". Synonyms: "Whatever happens, no matter what".

grammar.sentence: Suffice to say I was disappointed.
grammar.hint: Formal version requires "it" — "Suffice IT to say"
grammar.answer: Suffice it to say I was disappointed.
grammar.explanation: "Suffice it to say" — fossilised subjunctive with inverted "it". Loose modern usage often drops "it" ("suffice to say"), but the proper form keeps it. C1 writing prefers the full phrase.

grammar.passage: The ambassador chose his words. 'Be that as it may, the agreement stands. Come what may, neither side will retreat from what was signed. Suffice it to say that any party tempted to abandon the treaty would face consequences I shall not detail here.'
grammar.question: What does the ambassador imply about leaving the treaty?
grammar.answer: there would be undisclosed consequences (or "serious consequences")
grammar.explanation: Three fossilised subjunctives layered: "Be that as it may" (concession), "Come what may" (resolve), "Suffice it to say" (understatement). Diplomatic prose at its driest.

listening_speaking.text: Speak softly, lest you wake the baby.
Be that as it may, we must proceed.
Come what may, I'll be there.
Suffice it to say, the project is over.
So be it.

units.title: Mixed subjunctive
units.grammar_focus: Integration of mandative, hypothetical, fossilised subjunctive across registers
units.real_life_context: You select the subjunctive form that fits the register and intent.

grammar.sentence: I recommend that the candidate _____ a second interview.
grammar.explanation: Mandative subjunctive after "recommend that" — passive base form "be given". Base form of "to be" + past participle.

grammar.sentence: If she _____ here, this wouldn't have happened.
grammar.explanation: Third conditional — "had been" (past perfect subjunctive). "If she had been here" maps to a past unreal condition. Note: even with "she", we use "had been" not "would be".

grammar.sentence: It is essential that no exception _____ made.
grammar.explanation: "It is essential that + subject + be + past participle" — formal passive subjunctive. "Be made" — invariant. "Is made" would be indicative.

grammar.sentence: I suggested that he was more honest with his team.
grammar.hint: Mandative subjunctive requires base form, not past indicative
grammar.answer: I suggested that he be more honest with his team.
grammar.explanation: "Was" is indicative — it describes how he was, not what was suggested. The mandative trigger "suggested that" demands base form ("be") regardless of tense in the main clause.

grammar.passage: The professor closed her lecture with a quiet line: 'I would only ask that you remember three things. That you read what challenges you. That you write what scares you. And that, lest you become comfortable, you teach what you have only just begun to understand.' The room was silent for a long second.
grammar.question: What three things does she ask students to remember?
grammar.answer: read what challenges you, write what scares you, teach what you have only just begun to understand
grammar.explanation: Three mandative subjunctives ("that you read", "that you write", "that you teach"), capped by a "lest" subjunctive ("lest you become comfortable"). Layered C1 grammar in service of memorable speech.

listening_speaking.text: I suggest that he reconsider his approach.
It is vital that the policy be enforced.
I wish I were braver.
Come what may, I'll see it through.
Speak quietly, lest she overhear.

cross_unit_consolidation: Use mandative subjunctive after suggest, recommend, propose, demand, insist, require, urge ("that he be / go / take")
Apply subjunctive after impersonal evaluatives ("It is essential/vital/imperative that... be")
Maintain "were" universally in wishes, "if I were you", and "as if + subject"
Recognise and deploy fossilised subjunctive (Be that as it may, Come what may, Suffice it to say, So be it)
Choose between bare subjunctive and "should + base" (modern alternative)
